title: Derived sections on the basis detect isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme and $R$ a commutative ring. Use the small skeleton and universes of the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the constant sheaf of rings $R_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, the category of sheaves of $R_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $D^+(\mathcal A)$ be its bounded-below derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $\mathcal B_X$ be the affine ind-etale subsite of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For $W\in\mathcal B_X$, write $R\Gamma(W,-)$ for the right derived evaluation functor: represent an object by a bounded-below complex $I^\bullet$ of injective objects of $\mathcal A$ and take $\Gamma(W,I^\bullet)$ in $D^+(R_X(W)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$. Equivalently it is derived global sections after restriction to $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. If $u:K\to L$ is a morphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $R\Gamma(W,u)$ is an isomorphism for every $W\in\mathcal B_X$, then $u$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Work on the chosen small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its coefficient sheaf $R_X$ is commutative, so $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to $K$ and $L$ to obtain bounded-below complexes of injectives $I^\bullet,J^\bullet$ and isomorphisms $QI\simeq K$, $QJ\simeq L$. Both complexes are K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the conjugate of $u$ is represented by a homotopy class, hence by a chain map $a:I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$.

For each $W\in\mathcal B_X$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] identifies derived evaluation with derived global sections on the localized site. Since restriction preserves injectives, $\Gamma(W,I^\bullet)$ and $\Gamma(W,J^\bullet)$ compute these objects and $\Gamma(W,a)$ computes their morphism. By hypothesis its localized image is an isomorphism. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] in the abelian category of $R_X(W)$-modules shows that $H^n\Gamma(W,a)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $n$. Thus $\Gamma(W,a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $C^\bullet=C(a)$ be the ordinary mapping cone, so $C^n=J^n\oplus I^{n+1}$ and $d_C=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_J&a\\0&-d_I\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Evaluation preserves this finite direct sum and each displayed map, so $\Gamma(W,C)=C(\Gamma(W,a))$ as complexes. Apply [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] to $\Gamma(W,a)$ in the abelian category of $R_X(W)$-modules. Step 2 gives $H^n\Gamma(W,C)=0$ for every $W\in\mathcal B_X$ and every $n$. No exactness of evaluation on sheaves is asserted here.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), mapping cone construction; blueprint Proof: take the cone

proof.text: Regard $C^\bullet$ as a complex of presheaves of $R_X$-modules and set $P_n(U)=H^n(C^\bullet(U))$. Presheaf kernels and cokernels are objectwise, so $P_n=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ in presheaves. By exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], sheafifying this quotient gives the quotient of the sheafified kernel by the sheafified image. Since every $C^i$ is already a sheaf, this is exactly $\mathcal H^n(C)$, hence $P_n^\#\simeq\mathcal H^n(C)$. This is the explicit kernel-image calculation of Stacks 0BKV, applied to this complex; it does not claim $\mathcal H^n(C)(U)=P_n(U)$.

Fix $n$. Step 3 gives $P_n(W)=0$ for every basis object. For any sheaf of $R_X$-modules $F$ and presheaf morphism $b:P_n\to F$, any $U$ and $x\in P_n(U)$, cover $U$ by basis objects using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. On every member $W$ of that cover, $b_U(x)|_W=b_W(x|_W)=0$. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom gives $b_U(x)=0$. Thus every $b$ is zero. By the sheafification adjunction of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied with $F=P_n^\#$, both the identity and zero endomorphisms of $P_n^\#$ correspond to its zero unit map. They are equal, so $P_n^\#=0$. Step 4 implies $\mathcal H^n(C)=0$ for all $n$.

source.place: Proof: all these groups are zero on the basis, so every cohomology sheaf is zero; adjunction and sheaf separation supply the details

proof.text: Now $C(a)$ is acyclic as a complex in $\mathcal A$. Apply [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] in $\mathcal A$ to conclude that $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The localization $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], hence $Q(a)$ is an isomorphism. Conjugating back by $QI\simeq K$ and $QJ\simeq L$ proves that $u$ is an isomorphism.
